text: Hello everyone, welcome to my class.Today we are going to continue the topic of reading comprehension.Our focus today is text completion.By the end of the period, you are expected to know how to find clues based on the main idea and understand the logic in a close test to make the right choice.You are also expected to focus on the features of the text and overall structure to make a passage coherent by filling in appropriate sentences.In text completion, we will read a passage with missing words, phrases or sentences, and we are required to fill in each blank with a word, phrase or a proper sentence that best fits the context.Then, how to improve the accuracy?Actually, we don't make the choice as we please.We can focus on the main idea and the structure of the passage, rely on the logic in the context, and pay attention to the vocabulary at the same time.Yes, it sounds demanding.However, with the right strategies, I'm sure you can make progress.Now, would you please take out the assignment of the previous lesson?Let's check the answers first.If you've had some answers wrong, don't rush to correct them.Instead, analyze these mistakes first.Did you make the mistake because you didn't get the main idea and the structure of the passage?Or because you didn't keep them in mind when making the choices?Or was it because you failed to figure out the logic between different ideas?Or did you make the wrong choice because of your limited vocabulary?Next, we are going to focus on these aspects to improve our accuracy.The main idea is what the writer wants to convey to the readers.Most often, it serves as the purpose of writing this article, and all the following information is to support this purpose.So bearing the main idea in mind may help you a lot to find the clues of the missing parts.Can you recall what we've learned about how to find the main idea in the previous lesson?Yes, actually we skimmed the passage to get the main idea.Besides focusing on beginning and ending part, this time we can also pay attention to the title if there is one.Which can give us much information.The topic sentence in each paragraph and the keywords and signal words also serve the purpose.Now, please skim the passage to find the main idea.When you read, don't forget to leave some marks on the paper and try to find the relationship between the words.This is my version.Have you highlighted these words or phrases?What is the passage mainly about?It's about the scientist's study on marmoset monkeys' social practice.It takes a village.From the keywords, we learn that the writer describes a new study, gives us possible explanations and their conclusions of the result.The signal words but and yet rather show the transition of the content.With the help of these keywords, can you complete the mind map to learn the structure of the passage?Well, the subject of the study is marmoset monkeys.The scientists are studying the phenomenon of their social practice.This is actually a proverb in Africa, which means not only the baby's parents, but the whole villagers or the other members of the community will make efforts to raise babies.A new study focuses on their admirable community value, that is, being more likely to share food when alone with a baby.The two possible explanations for their selfless behavior are enhancing the status among peers, and paying the fees of group membership, or paying to stay.However, the test result shows that, in the case of marmoset monkeys, such practice is driven by a deep down motivation to help.Finding out the main idea and structure of a passage is half the battle.Whatever words go missing, we can find the clues within the sentence, between the sentences, or between the paragraphs.When we read the first paragraph, can you find the clues between the sentences?Please have a try.In the process of reading, it is important for us to sort out the hidden logic in the passage.I know you are quite familiar with the linking words in the options of blank one.Have you noticed the function of each linking word?However, it shows contrast.Moreover, it is usually followed by additional information.Otherwise, it shows a supposed condition, therefore indicates a result.According to the first sentence, we learn that marmoset monkeys are distinct from humans during evolution, indicating that they are not highly evolved, which forms a sharp contrast with pretty highly evolved in the second sentence.So A is obviously the right choice.And blank two, looking after babies, refers to parenting practices.So option D is the right one.You see, by relying on the clues of contrast and paraphrase, we can make the right choice.Then, is there any clue within the sentence?Let's try these two blanks.The first clue is the word further, which shows new study also proves the previous idea mentioned in the first paragraph.Although the original meaning of option A shine is to give out bright light, it can be interpreted as highlight.Compared with the other three options, it is closest in meaning to prove.So option A best fits the context.The second clue is the word then, showing here there is a comparison in comparison to being surrounded by other community members as being alone.In other words, in private, we choose option B.You see, in terms of vocabulary, sometimes you need to think about the implied meaning of the word.Signal words like then serve as a good reminder of logic.Sometimes the clues may not just lie between the sentences, they can also lie between the paragraphs.Please go through the following three blanks to see whether you can find the clues.With the main idea and structure in your mind, we know paragraph 2 tells us a new study showing that mamacet monkeys share their food more generously with little ones when they are alone with them.Here, generously is the clue, referring to the possible explanation of such behavior in paragraph 3.So generosity is the right choice.It is the repetition of the same idea.The next sentence is quite long.Have you noticed that it contains two clauses?Before rushing to find an answer, you need to analyze this long sentence first, making clear its structure and meaning.In the sentence, the first that is used to introduce an objective clause, while the second that is to introduce an adverbial clause.Focusing on the main structure, we learn that by showing he is good at getting material goods to give away, he enhances his power within the group.Option B, demonstrating, is closest in meaning here.In the last sentence, there is another that, but it is a reference word used as the subject of the sentence.Well, what is that here referring to?It refers to enhancing his power within the group.So, having more power, the monkey is very likely to attract a prospective or potential mate.We choose C.Appeal to means attract.After the previous analysis, would you try blank number 14?Can you find the clues from the previous paragraph?From the signal words all and rather, we learn that the two previously mentioned explanations, reputation management or avoidance of something, are not the reasons for the monkey's generous behavior.Here, reputation management refers to enhancing his power within the group in the previous paragraph.Then, the answer is clear.Exclusion from the group and a loss of potential partners refers to punishment.So here, we choose B.To improve our accuracy, we can try these steps when doing a close test.First, skim and figure out the main idea and structure of the passage while assuming the missing words.This is the first time reading, and we can focus more on the beginning and ending paragraphs, the topic sentence in each paragraph, the signal words and the key words.Next comes the second reading.Scan and choose the word or phrase that best fits the context based on logic and clues that lie within the sentence, between the sentences and the paragraphs.Third, read through the passage again and check for consistency and accuracy.What's more, when you practice, don't forget to build up your vocabulary, which is definitely of great help to your future reading.Now, let's move on to another kind of text completion.This time, what is missing is not the words but sentences.Besides the tips we mentioned above, do we have any other strategy to improve our reading?Let's take the following passage as an example.First, I think we can get clues from the options and title.You can leave different marks for different words.Reference words are the pronouns, such as this, referring to the information that appears before the sentence.Signal words are those indicating logic, such as understood, indicating a progressive relation.We underline the content words to help us find coherent information before or after the sentence.As for the words that appear repeatedly, they can tell us the topic of this passage.Here we can see the passage is about food.Now it's your turn to have a try.Well, have you found any other word that appears repeatedly?Yes, eating together, eating healthily.So, we can predict that the passage may be about eating with others and eating healthily.According to the title, this is most probably an argumentative writing.As to the content words, this is my version for your reference.Don't you see?Just by analyzing the title and options, we've already got a lot of information about this passage.Then, let's skim the passage to get the main idea.Please summarize each paragraph with one word to learn the structure of the passage.You can apply the method we've learned before.Did you find the important information on the worksheet as I did?Based on the key information, we learned that the first paragraph is the introduction of the topic, what does food mean to you?According to the sentence in the second paragraph, for me, food is family.The writer gives us his opinion.In the third paragraph, the topic sentence is missing, but from the supporting details like a lower risk and gives families a chance to reflect on their days together and forge stronger bonds, we learn this paragraph is about the benefits of eating together.Based on the transition words and the socio-familial aspect mentioned in the last paragraph, we know that this part is the restatement of the writer's opinion about food.In terms of the structure, it is typically an argumentative writing.After learning the structure, it is easy to find the proper missing sentence for blank number three.Here we need a sentence to outline the paragraph, which focuses on the benefits of eating together.So eight is the right choice with the key words, the importance of eating together.For the rest three blanks, you will have three minutes.Thank you for watching.Now let's look at the first paragraph.The signal word while shows a contrast here.The previous sentence must be related to some positive ideas about the inspiring books that encourage healthy eating.Which option contains such keywords?Yes, option D, books and healthy eating are mentioned in both sentences.So with the help of the signal word and the repetition of certain words, we can locate the proper sentence.Besides logic, sometimes the clue can be grammatical.Let's look at blank number two.Can you find the clues?Before the blank, we need to find the clue.Before the blank, would make, would share, would chat, never ate.The writer uses the past tense and the past future tense.While after the blank, with the word now, we find its plan.Here the writer uses the present tense.So the missing part should be a transitional sentence linking the past with the present.Which option contains such information?Yes, option F, were and are.And considering the whole paragraph is about food and meal time, we know F should be the proper one.As to the last paragraph, based on the previous analysis of the structure, it is the restatement of the writer's
